context.title: Obey God Rather Than Men
context.summary: Ananias and Sapphira lie about a gift and die. The apostles heal many, are jailed, are freed by an angel, and keep preaching. The respected teacher Gamaliel urges caution, and the apostles are beaten and released, rejoicing.
context.background: Gamaliel was a leading Pharisee and Paul's own teacher (22:3). He cites failed movements led by Theudas and by Judas of Galilee, who revolted at the census of AD 6. Josephus describes a Theudas in the mid-40s, which raises a well-known dating question.

customs.note: Synagogue and council floggings followed the law's limit of forty stripes, usually kept to thirty-nine (Deuteronomy 25:3; 2 Corinthians 11:24).

watchFor: 'Kept back' (v. 2) is the same word the Greek Old Testament uses for Achan's theft (Joshua 7:1).
'We ought to obey God rather than men' (v. 29).
They rejoiced to be 'counted worthy to suffer shame for his name' (v. 41).

people.name: Ananias
people.summary: One of the members of the church at Jerusalem, who conspired with his wife Sapphira to deceive the brethren, and who fell down and immediately expired after he had uttered the falsehood (Acts 5:5).

people.name: Holy Spirit
people.summary: The third Person of the adorable Trinity.

people.name: Simon
people.summary: Originally called Simon (=Simeon, i.e., “hearing”), a very common Jewish name in the New Testament. He was the son of Jona (Matt. 16:17). His mother is nowhere named in Scripture.

people.name: Satan
people.summary: Adversary; accuser. When used as a proper name, the Hebrew word so rendered has the article “the adversary” (Job 1:6-12; 2:1-7).

people.name: Jesus
people.also: Immanuel, Emmanuel, Messiah, Shiloh, Christ, Jesus Christ, Messias
people.summary: Anointed, the Greek translation of the Hebrew word rendered “Messiah”, the official title of our Lord, occurring five hundred and fourteen times in the New Testament.

people.name: Solomon
people.summary: Peaceful, (Heb. Shelomoh), David’s second son by Bathsheba, i.e., the first after their legal marriage (2 Sam. 12). He was probably born about B.C. 1035 (1 Chr. 22:5; 29:1).

people.name: Israel
people.summary: One who follows on another’s heels; supplanter, (Gen. 25:26; 27:36; Hos. 12:2-4), the second born of the twin sons of Isaac by Rebekah. He was born probably at Lahai-roi, when his father was fifty-nine and Abraham one hundred and fifty-nine years old.

people.name: Gamaliel
people.summary: The son of rabbi Simeon, and grandson of the famous rabbi Hillel. He was a Pharisse, and therefore the opponent of the party of the Sadducees.

people.name: Theudas
people.summary: Thanksgiving, referred to by Gamaliel in his speech before the council at Jerusalem (Acts 5:36). He headed an insurrection against the Roman authority.

places.name: Solomon's Portico
places.summary: (John 10:23; Acts 3:11; 5:12), a colonnade, or cloister probably, on the eastern side of the temple.

places.name: Jerusalem
places.summary: Called also Salem, Ariel, Jebus, the “city of God,” the “holy city;” by the modern Arabs el-Khuds, meaning “the holy;” once “the city of Judah” (2 Chr. 25:28).

events.title: Ananias and Sapphira lie to God
events.summary: Passage: Acts 5:1–11. People: God, Holy Spirit, Satan, Simon, Sapphira, Ananias. Place: Jerusalem.

events.title: Apostles work signs and wonders in Solomon's Portico
events.summary: Passage: Acts 5:12–17. People: Simon. Place: Solomon's Portico.

events.title: Apostles arrested, put on trial
events.summary: Passage: Acts 5:18–33. People: Simon. Place: Jerusalem.

events.title: Gamaliel advises the counsel and Apostles freed
events.summary: Passage: Acts 5:34–42. People: Gamaliel. Place: Jerusalem.
